chapter: Big band, Chicago players, recordings and gospel
title: Is there a Chicago style? Drive and competitiveness
summary: DeMichael thinks Chicago players play harder; Saunders says there is no formal style but musicians are hungrier and more competitive.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: And New Orleans is such a -- you know, they talk about New Orleans style, and Chicago style. Do you believe there's a Chicago style of playing jazz?

Well, at one time there may -- at one time I think there was. But I think most of the jazz today is just like if you go to New Orleans, you find -- you can find the same kind of jazz you find in Chicago or New York or anywhere. But they stick to their tradition. But Chicago had -- not now --
I don't mean what is normally called Chicago jazz, like Jimmy McPartland and those guys. I don't mean that.
Oh, yeah, no.
I mean generally. Is there a different way of playing here than in other places?
I don't think so. I think not.
I think there is. The Chicago player plays harder.
Yeah.
More rhythmically, sometimes. I was talking to Quinn about this.
Uh-huh.
And he always remarks about the rhythmic drive of the Earl Hines band compared to other bands.
Right, right.
We got talking about this, and not ever young musicians, since I've been up here, that have -- there's a hotness or --
Right, there is a --
-- more drive.
Drive, and a more of a -- see, jazz, to the way I -- I mean, I --
I don't mean a particular style. I mean just an approach.
Oh, oh, you mean that way. Yeah, right, the approach is different, because --
That's what I mean.
Yeah, right. I think the reason for that is because they're hungrier.
Well, it's almost as though the city --

Right, that's it. That's what I said, it's a hard driving city, but New York is hard driving, was, at one time. But they had a little more, and then the guys here, they're more competitive among themselves. They don't say it, but they are. Right, they're more competitive, and this makes good music.
That's right.
Right, it usually makes good music.
